reviews.evidence: Full source review: this is a navigation section whose body organizes independently defined Lie-group, Lie-algebra, representation, and structure-theory knowls; it introduces no mathematical object requiring prerequisites, so the empty list is correct.

Full source review: the core fixes a split semisimple Lie algebra, split Cartan subalgebra, root system, simple roots, and coroot pairing, then imposes the root-string normalization and integral-form relations. Those five concepts are direct inputs; later algebraic-group links are context.

Full theorem review: the statement classifies finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebras into the A–G families, so simple-lie-algebra is the direct hypothesis. Cartan/root/Dynkin links support the explanatory classification remarks and are not additional theorem inputs.

Full definition review: closedness is taken in the ambient Lie-group topology, with subgroup and closed-set structure as the remaining defining data. The explicit topological-space dependency was added.

Full theorem review: the hypotheses are a Lie group and a closed subgroup; the theorem constructs the embedded Lie-subgroup structure, identifies its Lie algebra, and supplies the smooth quotient manifold. The listed subgroup, closed-subgroup, Lie-subgroup, and Lie-algebra-of-subgroup concepts match those roles; quotient and smooth notions are theorem outputs named in the statement.

Full definition review: coadjoint action is the dual action on g* obtained from the adjoint representation of a Lie algebra. Lie algebra and adjoint representation are the only direct prerequisites; orbit and symplectic links occur in later applications.

Full definition review: [G,G] is generated by group commutators, so Lie-group and generated-subgroup are direct inputs. Normal subgroup and abelianization are equivalent characterizations/consequences, while the Lie-algebra statement is confined to remarks.

Full source review: the page fixes the compact connected simply connected simple group of E6 type and records rank, dimension, center, and compact real-form relation. Compact group, root system, Lie algebra, compact real form, and the E6 algebra are the direct identifying data; complexification is used in the explanatory form comparison.

Full source review: the page fixes the compact connected simply connected simple group of E7 type and records its rank, dimension, center, and real-form identification. The listed compact/root/Lie-algebra/compact-real-form/E7-algebra inputs are the direct identifying data; later Standard Model and generation links are context.

Full source review: the page identifies compact E8 by compact Lie-group structure, E8 root type, simple connectivity, Lie algebra, compact real form, and its weight-lattice distinction between forms. Those are direct inputs; Killing-form and E-series links support later remarks.

Full source review: the page identifies compact F4 by compactness, root type, simple connectivity, Lie algebra, compact real form, exceptional F4 algebra, and the Albert/Jordan model. The listed prerequisites supply these defining data; stabilizer and category links are later applications.

Full source review: the page identifies compact G2 by compactness, root type, simple connectivity, Lie algebra, compact real form, and the exceptional G2 algebra, then discusses octonion automorphisms as an example. The listed prerequisites cover the identification; stabilizer and algebraic-group links are contextual.

Full definition review: compactness is explicitly compactness of the underlying topological space of a Lie group. Topological-space was added as the direct ambient input; Haar measure, metrics, and representation results are remarks.

Full theorem/proof review: averaging starts with an inner product on the Lie algebra and Haar measure, then uses the adjoint action to produce an invariant inner product and bi-invariant metric. The added inner-product dependency is therefore direct; geodesics and volume forms are consequences.

Full theorem review: the decomposition requires a compact connected Lie group, its Lie-algebra center and semisimplicity criterion, and explicitly constructs a torus (compact connected abelian Lie group), a simply connected compact semisimple factor, and a finite central quotient. Abelian-lie-group was added for the torus factor; representation theory is context.

Full definition review: Sp(n) is the group of right quaternion-linear isometries of H^n, written by quaternionic matrices and then regarded as a Lie group. Vector space, quaternion division algebra, matrix, and Lie-group prerequisites directly supply the construction; SU(2) and the noncompact symplectic group are later comparisons.

Full definition review: the central quotient is constructed from the compact Sp(n), right Sp(1) action, and its image as a Lie subgroup; the kernel and Lie algebra are then computed. The listed compact-symplectic and Lie-subgroup inputs are direct, while holonomy is a later geometric application.

Full definition review: compatibility is exactly the intersection equation for Cartan subalgebras under an inclusion of Lie algebras. Cartan-subalgebra is the direct prerequisite; root-space and regular-subalgebra links are consequences of the compatibility condition.

Full definition review: a complementary-series member is selected from a normalized principal-series family for a real reductive group and required to be irreducible unitary. Those three listed prerequisites match the defining family, ambient group, and representation property; Knapp–Stein intertwiners and induced representations appear in later construction/context sections.

Full definition review: the core requires a field, a Lie algebra, a descending bracket-compatible filtration, and completeness; nilpotent quotients are developed in the pronilpotence section. The listed field/Lie-algebra/nilpotent inputs match the adopted convention, while BCH is a later consequence.

Full definition review: complete reducibility quantifies over every invariant subspace and requires an invariant complement, so operator-invariant-subspace is a direct input in addition to the representation and irreducibility notions. It was added; semisimplicity, compactness, and Weyl/Peter–Weyl links are later theorem context.

Full source review: the page defines sl3(C) by trace-zero complex 3x3 matrices and then records its A2 roots, Cartan, simple roots, and fundamental module. The existing simple, Dynkin, fundamental-representation, Cartan, simple-root, and matrix prerequisites cover those direct ingredients; group forms and tensor decompositions are later context.

Full source review: the page defines trace-zero 5x5 complex matrices and specifies A4 root data, Cartan/simple roots, and fundamental modules. The existing simple, Dynkin, fundamental-representation, Cartan, simple-root, and matrix prerequisites are direct; real/compact forms and E-series inclusions are contextual.

Full source review: the page defines trace-zero 6x6 complex matrices and specifies A5 root data, Cartan/simple roots, and fundamental modules. The existing six prerequisites provide those direct ingredients; E7 branching and global forms are later applications.

Full source review: the page defines so10(C) as infinitesimal preservers of a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form and identifies its D5/simple structure and half-spin modules. Bilinear-form, Lie-algebra, simple, Dynkin, and half-spin prerequisites are direct; spin groups and E6 branching are later context.

Full source review: the page defines so12(C) from a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form, then gives D6 structure and half-spin modules. The existing Lie-algebra, bilinear-form, simple, Dynkin, and half-spin inputs match; E7 branching is contextual.

Full definition review: a complex Lie group requires a complex manifold with holomorphic multiplication and inversion, and its morphisms are holomorphic group homomorphisms. The three listed prerequisites supply exactly these data; tangent algebra and examples are later sections.

Full construction review: complexification is h tensor_R C with the uniquely extended bracket and the embedded real Lie subalgebra. Tensor-product is a direct construction input and was added; the universal property and realification comparison are later material.

Full definition review: the core map (g,h)↦ghg^{-1} is explicitly the algebraic conjugation action and is then checked as a smooth action. The algebra-groups conjugation-action prerequisite was added alongside Lie-group and smooth-action inputs; orbit, centralizer, and adjoint links are later properties.

Full theorem review: the classification assumes a connected abelian Lie group and uses its Lie algebra, universal cover, discrete kernel, and exponential map to obtain R^n×T^m. The existing prerequisites cover these hypotheses and proof mechanism; circle/torus examples are context.

Full definition review: connectedness is imposed on the underlying topology of a Lie group, with connected-set supplying the property. The existing prerequisites are sufficient; identity component, normal subgroup, and exponential-map statements are structural consequences/remarks.

Full theorem review: uniqueness is for connected immersed Lie subgroups of a Lie group with equal Lie subalgebras. The existing Lie-group, Lie-subgroup, and Lie-subalgebra prerequisites are exactly the hypotheses; exponential generation is proof context.

Full definition review: the page starts with a maximal torus character/cocharacter pairing and root datum coroots, then defines reflections and dominance. The maximal-torus weight-lattice and root-data prerequisites are direct; simple roots, Borel, and Langlands duality are later uses.

Full definition review: G/H is constructed with quotient topology and, for closed Lie subgroups, smooth manifold structure and transitive action. Quotient-topology and smooth-structure are direct; homogeneous-space remains an explanatory link to preserve the foundational DAG.

Full definition review: a covering Lie-group map is a smooth homomorphism whose underlying topological map is a covering map; connectedness then yields discrete central kernel and Lie-algebra isomorphism. Topological-space and group-homomorphism were added as direct inputs; universal-cover material is later.

Full definition review: cyclicity is defined by the closed span of an orbit for a strongly continuous unitary representation, with closed-linear-subspace and cyclic-vector notions supplying the direct ingredients. GNS and coefficient facts are later sections.

Full definition review: the defining representation is the inclusion action of a matrix Lie algebra on its underlying vector space. Lie-algebra and matrix prerequisites directly support the core; bilinear forms, highest weights, and spin-group comparisons occur later.

Full definition review: a derivation is a linear endomorphism satisfying Leibniz for the Lie bracket, and derivations inherit the commutator Lie-algebra structure. The Lie-algebra prerequisite supplies the ambient bracket/vector structure; inner/outer derivations and automorphism motivation are later.

Full definition review: dπ differentiates π(exp(tX)) on the common invariant smooth-vector domain. Operator-invariant-subspace and exponential-map were added because both the domain and the defining curve occur in the core; Stone, enveloping-algebra, and equivariance results are later sections.

Full definition review: the derived series starts with a Lie algebra and repeatedly takes its derived subalgebra, with ideal structure stated afterward. The existing Lie-algebra, derived-subalgebra, and ideal prerequisites directly support the definition; solvability and group analogies are later.

Full definition review: a free action is defined by trivial stabilizer at every point for a smooth Lie-group action. Lie group, smooth action, and stabilizer are direct prerequisites; orbit/properness and principal-bundle remarks are consequences.

Full definition review: fundamental representations are finite-dimensional irreducible highest-weight modules of a complex semisimple Lie algebra, with weights dual to simple coroots. Semisimple-lie-algebra was added as the missing ambient hypothesis; the remaining listed root, Cartan, and highest-weight concepts are direct.

Full definition review: the boundary is G/P for a connected noncompact real semisimple Lie group and minimal parabolic P, with compact homogeneous-space structure and K/M identification supplied by Langlands and Iwasawa decompositions. The listed group, parabolic, homogeneous-space, decomposition, and maximal-compact inputs match the construction.

Full definition review: a (g,K)-module requires a vector space, complexified Lie-algebra action, compact subgroup action with K-finiteness, and compatibility. The listed Lie group, Lie algebra, vector space, Lie representation, and K-finite-vector concepts supply these data; enveloping algebra and globalization are later.

Full theorem review: Gårding density smooths a strongly continuous unitary representation by compactly supported smooth functions integrated against Haar measure, producing dense Gårding and smooth-vector spaces. Haar measure was added as a direct analytic input; the derived representation is a consequence.

Full definition review: the Gårding space is the span of integrated operators π(f) for compactly supported smooth f, using Haar measure and a strongly continuous unitary representation. The existing four prerequisites directly supply the group, measure, representation, and integrated form.

Full definition review: a Gelfand pair is a locally compact group with compact subgroup whose bi-invariant convolution algebra, defined using Haar measure, is commutative. Locally compact group, Haar measure, and homogeneous-space inputs are appropriate; multiplicity-free representation statements are later equivalences.

Full definition review: GL(V) is the group of invertible linear endomorphisms of a finite-dimensional real or complex vector space. Vector-space, linear-map, group, dimension/basis, and determinant prerequisites cover the adopted finite-dimensional matrix-group setting; no later Lie structure is needed in the core.

Full definition review: gl(V) is End(V) with the commutator Lie bracket. Vector-space and Lie-bracket prerequisites directly supply the ambient endomorphism space and bracket; matrix coordinates are explanatory.

Full theorem/construction review: each V_k is defined from the E7 root projection class and then identified with the even exterior algebra of the defining module. The missing E7-root-projection-trichotomy input was added; exterior algebra, vector-space, and subalgebra concepts remain direct.

Full definition review: the generation plane is the real span of the A2 root system arising from a specified good embedding, generation algebra, and compatible Cartans. The existing good-embedding, generation-sl3, compatible-Cartan, root-system, and Cartan inputs are direct.

Full definition review: the three generation sl2 subalgebras are assembled from opposite roots and Cartan elements inside the generation plane, using the root-sl2 construction. Generation-plane and root-sl2-subalgebra are direct prerequisites.

Full definition review: the generation sl3 is the unique Lie subalgebra in the centralizer of a fixed good Standard Model embedding in e7. Good embedding, centralizer, Lie-subalgebra, and Lie-algebra prerequisites directly state the construction.

Full theorem review: the K×p→G map is k exp X, with K and the Cartan decomposition supplied by the real reductive hypotheses. Exponential-map was added because the exponential is part of the theorem’s defining displayed map; KAK refinement is later.

Full definition review: the global character is the distribution f↦Tr π(f) for an admissible finite-length globalization, with Haar measure and integrated operators. The existing Lie-group, Haar, admissibility, integrated-operator, and distribution prerequisites directly support the definition.

Full definition review: goodness specifies an automorphism class of regular embeddings of the complexified Standard Model algebra into e7 obtained via root removal and a maximal Levi. The listed Standard Model, e7, regular, root-removal, and Levi concepts are direct; the SU(5) route is an optional equivalent construction.

Full definition review: an oriented even-dimensional complex quadratic space with Clifford algebra spinor module and chirality operator splits into the two half-spin modules. The five listed quadratic/Clifford/chirality/spinor prerequisites directly supply the construction; highest-weight and real-form material is later.

Full theorem review: for a real reductive group and maximal compact subgroup, every irreducible unitary representation has finite multiplicity for each K-type. Real-reductive, maximal-compact, irreducible-unitary, and K-type prerequisites exactly match the hypotheses and conclusion.

Full definition review: the c-function is defined by a Haar-normalized integral over the opposite nilpotent subgroup using an Iwasawa projection and restricted-root half-sum. Lie group, Iwasawa decomposition, restricted roots, and Haar measure are direct inputs; asymptotics and Plancherel density are later properties.

Full theorem review: the criterion assumes a connected semisimple real Lie group with finite center and maximal compact subgroup, and equates discrete series with compact Cartan and equal ranks. The listed Lie-group, maximal-compact, and discrete-series concepts support the stated theorem; examples and rank interpretation are explanatory.
Full theorem review: the Harish–Chandra map uses semisimple g, Cartan/positive roots, Z(U(g)), and Weyl invariants, and its construction explicitly invokes PBW; PBW was added.

Full source review: the page defines a Harish–Chandra module as an admissible (g,K)-module finitely generated over U(g); the five listed real-reductive, maximal-compact, (g,K), admissibility, and enveloping prerequisites are direct.

Full source review: V_K is constructed from K-finite vectors of an admissible finite-length representation, with differentiated g-action and K-action; the listed six prerequisites supply each construction datum.
Full theorem review: invariant eigendistributions are defined using invariant differential operators from Z(U(g)); center-of-universal-enveloping-algebra was added.

Full theorem review: the classification assumes a complex semisimple Lie algebra plus Cartan, positive/simple roots, and highest-weight notions; semisimple-lie-algebra was added.
